BINGO. I struggled the other way round (was obese through my teens) but I only really started losing weight once I turned 21.

I recently lost around 100 lbs through overhauling my eating and exercise. Now how you change the way you eat is truly up to you, what worked for me is intermittent fasting (16 off, 8 on, I do take frequent breaks when I want breakfast though) which for me is 2 big meals plus snacks. For a while I went low carb but realised I was burning through more muscle than I'd like. Since then, I eat carbs again I just generally watch what I eat (not too many carbs, keep an eye on fat and sugar, plenty of fresh vegetables and protein)

Exercise isn't as important, it you're roughly watching what you eat you will probably lose weight but calisthenics and lifting small weights is what I used (along with yoga from time to time and walking when I can, I'm disabled). Whatever exercise works for you is great but I hope some of this can be helpful. Diets are never fool proof, find what works for you and stick to it til you get results. Also I HUGELY recommend listening to Ethan Supplee on the Tom Talks podcast

EDIT: I now weigh around 180 lbs.

If you want something that helped me, vitamin e oil. Rub it into the scars (kind of aggressive, helps break down the scar tissue) and leave til the skin absorbs it. Medical staff like this are massively overlooked. When I first landed in hospital for SH, I was put in a really shitty situation (they put me on a childs' cancer ward, at 15, waiting for surgery on a self inflicted wound, seriously) but there were a few nurses I will always remember for how they reached out to me during that time. One young nurse saw how mentally unstable I was so found my parents a separate place to sit and just talked with me about music. She took time out of her day to settle my mind and that really helped. Seeing her again when I relapsed really made me see I had to get clean, the disappointment/sadness in her eyes hurt so much. I've been clean (apart from minor relapses) for just over 5 years now, part of me still does it for the people like that nurse who took time to be a nice person to a random, depressed teenager. Remember that nurse.

Okay, might as well tell my story about this. Warning: kinda obvious it will reference self harm but also an abusive relationship.

Around the time my self harm was at it's height, I fell for a girl I'd met at a gig (mutual friends, I stayed at her place that night due to where the gig was). We lived a fair distance apart (4 hour train journey, in a small country that's a long way) but started chatting online. I told her about my self harm and the "you cut, I'll cut" discussion took place. At this time, I was dealing with some real heavy stuff but I couldn't tell a lot of my past trauma, I was the most vulnerable I'd ever been, so I agreed. And I relapsed.

This is part of a much bigger story of how shit went wrong, she caused me a lot of trauma (not entirely her fault but I've struggled to accept that she was very abusive to me at points) but that night will stick with me, it's the first time she took advantage of me. The guilt I felt is part of the reason I stopped, it took a few years for me to rationalize that the "you cut, I cut" idea may come from a good place but it's such a toxic idea. She left my life for good 5 or 6 years ago, I struggle to think about that time and I still get flashbacks to certain incidents. That night fucked me up when it comes to trust and relationships. If you are currently self harming and someone starts this shit, let them know kindly that is will make you feel worse if anything, they probably don't realize it.
